function: Prediction of future compressed CSI (P steps ahead from K=12 past steps) with an evolving-graph GNN, then decoder reconstruction, for channel aging in massive MIMO (p. 1-3).
system: Single-cell MIMO-OFDM system, BS dual-polarized UPA with Nt=32 antennas (8x2x2), single-antenna UE, 32 subcarriers, 20 MHz, UMa, 3-120 km/h; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2-3).
method: ERAN spatio-temporal GNN: evolving graph learning with matrix GRUs, temporal attentional convolution, diffusion graph convolution; supervised RMSE loss, Adam, 200 epochs; STNet-based CSI encoder/decoder (p. 3-5).
data_channel: Sionna-generated 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa channels: 160,000 samples, split 120,000 train, 20,000 validation, 20,000 test (p. 5).
test_conditions: Train: 120,000 of 160,000 UMa samples, K=12 history; test: 20,000 held-out samples, reported at 3, 30, 120 km/h, C 128-512, P 3-12; per-mobility training not stated (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned only: STEM GNN (spectral-temporal GNN, earlier work), LSTM, Transformer; same STNet-based encoder/decoder; no classical predictor (p. 4).
metrics: RMSE of predicted compressed CSI (horizons P=3-12); spectral efficiency with ZF precoding versus Eb/N0 and mobility; runtime and parameter counts (p. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(C^2 d + C d^2), simplified to O(C^2), versus O(C^3) for STEM; Table II: ERAN C=512 0.0186 s, 2.48M parameters; C=128 0.0043 s, 0.68M (p. 2, 5).
q1_support: p. 5: "A 3GPP-compliant Urban Macro (UMa) scenario based on TR 38.901 is simulated"; p. 2: "The 3D wireless channel is modeled as 3GPP spatial channel model (SCM) for 5G [16]".
q2_support: p. 5: "120,000 are used for training, 20,000 for validation, and 20,000 for testing", a held-out part of the same data. Results are shown at 3, 30 and 120 km/h, but the paper never states that a model trained under one mobility or scenario is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 4: "We benchmark ERAN against SOTA data-driven baselines" (STEM GNN, LSTM, Transformer). All baselines are learned; no non-learned predictor, such as outdated CSI or an autoregressive model, is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "Model complexity is further detailed in Table II, comparing parameter counts and inference times." Table II lists runtime and parameters for ERAN, and the text gives the order O(C^2) versus O(C^3) for STEM.
q5_support: p. 5: "We use the Sionna ray-tracing simulator" "for dataset generation". The authors generate their own 160,000 samples with an open-source library; no link to their code or dataset is given.
notes: Area 2 (CSI prediction with feedback compression). q3 is 0 only because there is no non-learned baseline: STEM GNN, LSTM and Transformer are all learned (p. 4), and Fig. 3 legends list only ERAN, STEM, TRANS and LSTM. q5 is 0: Sionna is an open-source simulator, not a released dataset, and no code or data link appears; reviewer may confirm. q1: the paper calls Sionna a ray-tracing simulator but states the scenario is 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa (p. 5). q2: the split of the 160,000 samples across the three mobilities is not described and per-mobility training is not stated, so no unseen-condition test is explicit. BS has 32 antennas and the UE one (MISO), so the link is not single-antenna at both ends. All 5 pages read, Tables I-II and Figs. 3-5 viewed as images.
